A.description: matcher before D21: one IN-list load of every candidate, validate every patient, one result dict per patient

B.description: D21 step 1: chunked load and match, PreparedQuery, trusted events, integer window checks, SQL comparability; then the engine kernel: closed-form pair and unary tests over per-patient records, Times and events built without per-call overhead (results unchanged); then time pruning on the posting summaries (D25): a candidate the summaries prove `none` gets the engine's own `none` without loading its events (results unchanged); detail='full'

B_unpruned.description: arm B with time pruning on the posting summaries (D25) turned off (`execution_store._PRUNE = False`): the same tree, as a same-run baseline; its results must equal B's byte for byte

C.description: D21 arm C: B plus partition-parallel matching in a persistent pool of spawned worker processes, at 1, 2, 4, 8, 14 workers; detail='full'

D.description: Rust matcher, single-threaded and batched, including FFI (a later change, built only if B+C misses the target)

D'.description: Rust matcher, parallel (a later change, same condition)

limitations: One machine (see environment); no other hardware, operating system or storage was measured.
The data are synthetic and replicated beyond 10,000 distinct patients (see the scaling report): candidate sets and outcomes scale as exact multiples, which a real population would not.

Queries are the scaling benchmark's seeded random queries (10 at 100,000 patients and above), not a clinical mix; percentiles over 10 queries rest on few samples, and the maximum is the slowest single query.

Arm A is the code of the stated git ref extracted and imported from a scratch directory; both arms read the same snapshot files. The snapshots were built by the builder at the ref the report states, not by the final tree. Arm A's code reads execution store 2.0; it opens the 2.1 snapshots (D24, which only added columns) as the same files under a manifest relabelled 2.0 (`snapshot_view` in its arm entries), which is refused unless no patient shares variables and no event is proper or names a variable; the synthetic cohorts use none of them.

Peak memory is the query process's maximum resident set size. It includes the interpreter, DuckDB buffers, the caller's windows dictionary (one entry per patient, rebuilt for each query) and the full result, which for detail='full' is one dict per patient and is part of what the caller asked for.

"Engine-only" time is the seconds inside `trajectory_graph` match calls as measured by a wrapper (about 0.1 microsecond of overhead per call); "end-to-end" is the whole `match` call including candidates(), loading, comparability, exclusions and the context digests.
Latencies are wall-clock times of one Python thread and one DuckDB thread; no tuning was attempted.

Byte identity is checked by a digest of canonical JSON of the plan, candidate count, counts and every patient result (not the context block, whose snapshot and code digests change with the code); no exhaustive reference ran at scale.

Arm C: workers and the query process share one machine (10 performance and 4 efficiency cores): counts above 10 put work on efficiency cores. Workers are warm for the timings; start-up is one cold figure per count, with the page cache warm from earlier arms. The comparability and exclusion steps still run in the query process.
Arms D and D' have not been run.

confirmation.note: Arms B and B_unpruned ran once (digests and per-candidate reference); arm C at each count with the repeats stated. "all_runs" pools every (query, repeat) measurement; per-query figures elsewhere are medians over repeats.
